_about: The dashboard To-Do feed. Refreshed at every Rule 8 checkpoint alongside the session handoff — this is the handoff distilled into plain language for the 📋 button on every tab. Split For Sam (curation / decisions only a human makes) and For Fable (engineering, the next session picks up).
_as_of: 2026-08-19 · Sky168 — the GR register was audited hard, the things it had quietly dropped are back, and the GR phrase no longer opens the whole workplan.
_status: Two things shipped. First, every COBI page now carries a plain notice that it is an experimental data suite in Alpha development, and '(Alpha)' rides in the page title so a link pasted into Teams or Slack says so before anyone clicks. Second, the GR Priorities tab was rebuilt for the General Counsel demo. It used to be one fixed document about one topic that nobody could add to. It is now a register: you pick a priority area, you see the revisions under consideration with the exact Title 5 or Ed. Code sections they touch, you can search and filter them, and you can add new areas, revisions and source documents yourself. The section filters only became possible because the legal citations were pulled out of the prose and made into real data — and that unlocked something nobody asked for: the tab can now show when two different priority areas are both proposing to change the same section, which is the kind of collision that otherwise only surfaces during rulemaking. One thing to know before the demo: the GR phrase currently also opens every shared team tab, so General Counsel cannot be given a phrase until that is scoped.

items.text: One thing to check: the GR phrase no longer opens the shared team tabs — it never needed to, and it was opening 42 tables it has no use for. If anyone holds ONLY the GR phrase, they will have lost the Workplan and the rest and should be given the shared team phrase. Undoing it is a one-line change if that is easier.

The CPL area says 0 of 16 entries have had their citations checked against the primary source. That is honest — the citations were pulled out of the prose by machine and nobody has confirmed them. Open a row and press 'Mark citations verified' as you check each one; the tab counts them off, and the warning banner can retire once they are all done.

Open the GR tab (?org=gr) and walk it as if you were General Counsel. Pick the Dual Enrollment sample area — it is deliberately neutral prompts, not our positions — then switch to CPL. Save the cross-area section list for last; it is the thing they cannot get from a folder of Word documents.

Worth considering: drop the shared phrase for GR entirely and use sign-in instead. A shared phrase cannot say who read or changed anything, cannot be revoked for one person, and can be guessed. Everyone who needs GR would need a sign-in account first — tell us who that is and we can check them before anything changes.

A bigger idea to react to: which sections are under review is public law, but our position on them is not. We have built the switch to separate the two, defaulted to closed so nothing changed. Flipping it would let the whole Chancellor's Office see the section list while positions stay private — that is what would make this a CO tool rather than a MAP tool.

Send the authoritative list of Chancellor's Office priority areas when you have it (CPL, dual enrollment, baccalaureates, SCFF, climate, professional development, financial aid…). Until then anyone signed in can type an area title straight into the tab.

Add editing. Right now you can add an area, a revision or an artifact but you cannot change or delete one, and a review workflow is mostly revising. The history table and triggers that record who changed what are already live and waiting for it.

Sierra's document knowledge base was last indexed on 19 July and is fed from your private vault by a tool outside this project. If General Counsel starts contributing documents, that pipeline needs an owner — right now it does not appear to have one.

Two of the five choices on My College are switched off: Strong Workforce region and Academic Senate region. We could not find either grouping in anything we hold — you said they are on the MAP Dashboard. If you can get us a list of which college belongs to which, both switch on the same day. We deliberately did NOT guess from the region data we do have, because it is a different set of boundaries and would have quietly put colleges in the wrong group.

The new My College briefing downloads as a Word document named starting with the date (20260817_...). The older Custom Report puts its date at the end instead. Worth picking one so your folder sorts properly — say which and we will make them match.

Sierra now uses plain words instead of emoji everywhere she appears. But the Fact Sheet's own buttons still have them (the Word and Print buttons), so that row now has one plain button between two with icons. Same for the To-Do and signed-in labels on every tab. Say the word and we will finish the sweep — it is a few minutes.

You said 115 credit colleges and 4 noncredit campuses. The 115 matches exactly. We can only find 3 noncredit — North Orange Continuing Education, San Diego College of Continuing Education, and Calbright. The fourth is Mt. SAC's noncredit side, and it does not exist as its own entry anywhere in MAP, so it cannot be a column until it does. Worth deciding whether MAP should carry it separately.
